question: Who leads the government in the UK?
options: The Speaker of the House of Commons
explanation: The Prime Minister leads the government with the support of the Cabinet and ministers. The Prime Minister is ultimately responsible for all policy and decisions.

question: What is the Cabinet?
options: The judges of the Supreme Court
The heads of the Civil Service
explanation: The Cabinet is made up of the senior members of government. Its members are Secretaries of State from all departments and some other ministers.

options: The practical and administrative work of government

question: What is a Bill?
options: A law that has already been passed
A report by a government department
A proposal for a new law or a change to an existing one
explanation: Bills are proposals for new laws or changes to existing ones. The House of Commons and the House of Lords work together to make laws.

source.title: How government works (GOV.UK)
source.quote_under_25_words: Bills are proposals for new laws or changes to existing ones.

question: After Parliament has agreed a Bill, who has to approve it before it becomes law?
options: The Speaker of the House of Commons
explanation: A Bill agreed by Parliament has to be approved by the monarch before it becomes law. GOV.UK names the King.

source.title: How government works (GOV.UK)
source.quote_under_25_words: Once agreed by Parliament, they have to be approved by the King before becoming law.

exam_version: Life in the UK Test (24 questions; official handbook not in the pack)
question: What is an Act of Parliament?
options: A speech by the Prime Minister
A proposal that has not yet been debated
A Bill that has been approved by the Commons, the Lords and the King
A rule made by a local council
explanation: Acts of Parliament are Bills that have been approved by both Houses and by the monarch. The relevant government department is responsible for putting the Act into practice.

source.title: How government works (GOV.UK)
source.quote_under_25_words: These are bills which have been approved by the Commons, the Lords, and the King.
